papers.title: Quantifying and Visualizing Uncertainties in Molecular Models
papers.abstract: Computational molecular modeling and visualization has seen significant progress in recent years with sev- eral molecular modeling and visualization software systems in use today. Nevertheless the molecular biology community lacks techniques and tools for the rigorous analysis, quantification and visualization of the associated errors in molecular structure and its associated properties. This paper attempts at filling this vacuum with the introduction of a systematic statistical framework where each source of structural uncertainty is modeled as a ran- dom variable (RV) with a known distribution, and properties of the molecules are defined as dependent RVs. The framework consists of a theoretical basis, and an empirical implementation where the uncertainty quantification (UQ) analysis is achieved by using Chernoff-like bounds. The framework enables additionally the propagation of input structural data uncertainties, which in the molecular protein world are described as B-factors, saved with almost all X-ray models deposited in the Protein Data Bank (PDB). Our statistical framework is also able and has been applied to quantify and visualize the uncertainties in molecular properties, namely solvation interfaces and solvation free energy estimates. For each of these quantities of interest (QOI) of the molecular models we provide several novel and intuitive visualizations of the input, intermediate, and final propagated uncertainties. These methods should enable the end user achieve a more quantitative and visual evaluation of various molecular PDB models for structural and property correctness, or the lack thereof.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文讨论了分子结构的不确定性量化，与有限元代理模型及生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on molecular protein models and uses Chernoff-like bounds for UQ, with no finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, or implant/biomechanics context.

summary_zh.motivation: 分子建模中缺乏系统的不确定性量化与可视化工具。
summary_zh.method: 提出统计框架，将结构不确定性建模为随机变量并传播。
summary_zh.result: 实现了溶剂界面和自由能的不确定性量化与可视化。
summary_zh.validation: 基于蛋白质数据库的结构数据验证。

summary_en.motivation: The molecular modeling community lacks rigorous methods for quantifying and visualizing uncertainties in molecular structures and properties.
summary_en.method: A statistical framework treats each structural uncertainty source as a random variable and propagates it to property uncertainties using Chernoff-like bounds.
summary_en.result: Novel visualizations of input, intermediate, and final uncertainties are provided for solvation interfaces and free energy estimates.
summary_en.validation: The framework is demonstrated on X-ray models from the Protein Data Bank.

papers.title: 3D bioprinting of neural stem cell-laden thermoresponsive biodegradable polyurethane hydrogel and potential in central nervous system repair
papers.first_author_affiliation: Institute of Polymer Science and Engineering, National Taiwan University, Taipei, Taiwan

corresponding_authors.name: Shan‐hui Hsu
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Institute of Polymer Science and Engineering, National Taiwan University, Taipei, Taiwan; Research Center for Developmental Biology and Regenerative Medicine, National Taiwan University, Taipei, Taiwan; Research and Development Center for Medical Devices, National Taiwan University, Taipei, Taiwan. Electronic address: shhsu@ntu.edu.tw

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及3D生物打印，但未集成AI，与用户AI驱动生物打印的方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not integrate AI into any bioprinting workflow stage, lacking machine learning or autonomous decision-making components.

summary_zh.motivation: 构建用于中枢神经修复的神经干细胞负载水凝胶支架。
summary_zh.method: 使用温敏可降解聚氨酯水凝胶进行3D生物打印包埋神经干细胞。
summary_zh.result: 成功打印出保持高活力和分化能力的细胞负载支架。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞培养和表征验证支架的生物相容性。

summary_en.motivation: To create a cell-laden scaffold for central nervous system repair using 3D bioprinting.
summary_en.method: Neural stem cells were encapsulated in a thermoresponsive biodegradable polyurethane hydrogel and printed into constructs.
summary_en.result: Printed scaffolds maintained high cell viability and supported neural differentiation.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and characterization including viability assays and immunofluorescence.
